page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY processor cores running at 2.5 GHz, with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and there are no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.e3.large delivers modest compute and memory performance. The Intel Xeon 8269CY CPU scored in the bottom 25% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as Geekbench and PassMark CPU evaluations. While the processor supports AVX and AVX-512F instructions, it lacks newer vector and matrix extensions like AVX-512 VNNI or AMX. Memory performance is mixed; read-only bandwidth for both small and large blocks is weak, though large-block write bandwidth achieves an average rating in the middle 50%. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, fall into the bottom 10% of tested hardware.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.e3.large is its high memory allocation relative to its lower-tier compute performance. With database operations and Redis SET benchmarks performing in the bottom tier, this instance is less suited for high-throughput transactional databases. However, its qualitative cost efficiency lies in providing a dense 32.0 GB memory footprint without the premium cost of high-performance compute cores. It is appropriate for memory-intensive workloads that do not require intense CPU processing, such as caching layers, lightweight memory-bound applications, and basic data buffering.
